traits.perianth.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 424: perianth dichlamydeous, a fused 4-5 (2) lobed calyx and a fused corolla.

traits.carpels.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 424: ovary of 2, rarely 3, carpels (Floral Diagrams p. 328: G2).

traits.ovary_position.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 424: flowers hypogynous with a superior ovary.

traits.hypanthium.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 424, 505: Simpson calls the flowers hypogynous. Simpson p. 505 defines hypogynous and epigynous as flowers without a hypanthium.

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 324 Scrophulariaceae (its core: Verbascum, Scrophularia, Nemesia, Sutera), 227 Buddleiaceae, 339 Myoporaceae and 340 Selaginaceae, which APG joins as Scrophulariaceae (Hutchinson's figwort family also held what APG puts in Plantaginaceae and Orobanchaceae): herbs or shrubs, rarely small trees; leaves alternate, opposite or whorled; no stipules; flowers mostly irregular, the butterfly bushes' regular; corolla united, a tube of 4 or 5 lobes, often two-lipped; stamens 4 (two long, two short) or 2, rarely 5; ovary superior, of two cells; fruit a capsule, the myoporums' a drupe. The order (Lamiales) states the stipules, the ovary and the two carpels.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Scrophulariaceae with Buddlejaceae, Ellisiophyllaceae, Linderniaceae, Myoporaceae, Orobanchaceae: its irregular flowers have a two-lipped corolla, read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy bilabiate.

traits.leaf_division.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 424, 425, family Scrophulariaceae: leaf division simple; read as "simple".

traits.stipules.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 424, 425, family Scrophulariaceae: stipules false; read as false.

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 424, 425, family Scrophulariaceae: inflorescence spike, raceme or thyrse; read as {"panicle": "often", "raceme": "often", "spike": "often"}.

traits.fruit_type.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add berry (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 424, 425: capsule, drupe or berry.
